item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: "Straightforward thriller" and "man versus the supernatural" have been popular narratives since 2100 BCE. We aren't going to use it up here, I don't think.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Yeah, in theory, a plethora of stories like this could be told. However, there reaches a point where people are going to think, "didn't that guy do this already?" and they'll give five examples. My point is not that it's a bad story, or too basic a plot; my point is that this tale is innovative, and should be, if ever built off of, only in moderation, to preserve the great storytelling this creates. If you see the "This is Sparta" remix, and then you watch the hundreds of cheap, poorly composed knockoffs, the knockoffs begin to make you lose respect for the original thing. So let's just appreciate this story for what it is, not what people could make out of it.

item.title: Plot Hole
item.content:encoded: Wasn't it stressed that any shadows could be created by something minute as lifting his foot? How would it be safe to set down the box - when a large box could easily create a shadow - to take out the light bulb? Why would he even need to be sent in with the light bulb in the box? Wouldn't they just send him in with the light bulb outright? I admit, it adds another degree of fear and tension, but at the cost of a break of the laws you already established two paragraphs ago.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is a story about a minor technical issue that is quickly resolved and ends up with nobody dead.

And yet, there is thrill here. I echo Kalinin's words from before; there is information within some of the longer paragraphs that feels bulky and breaks up what is otherwise really, really good flow. This, I think, can be excused, because the rest of the tale is very good. There's a real feeling of insecurity throughout the whole thing that makes a reader uncomfortable, and the imagery used practically invites claustrophobia.

Is it revolutionizing the Foundation? No. Is it a life or death drama with everything on the line? Not unless you're the technician, no. But is it just as thrilling as all of the other great tales on the wiki, and does it highlight the inherent danger that sometimes gets overlooked?

Yes. I'd say it does that very well.

What utter irony it would be, for one containment breach to occur because the efforts of preventing a breach interfered with another object's containment!

Heh, I see what you did there (I think).

Anyway, I liked this a lot. You get so used to incident reports and interview logs sometimes you forget that there's a real story behind it.

Lloyd Swinburne nodded, feel more drained than he had ever been.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm very close to upvoting. The writing was done well enough to keep me interested, and the level of detail of how the site and 017's containment chamber worked added some nice immersion. I didn't much care for the detailed background on the characters; it broke the flow of the story, and if knowing these guys' histories was essential (I'd say it's probably more relevant to the dude changing the bulb), it may have been better to communicate that in ways other than stopping the action cold and giving us a paragraph.

Neutral vote for now, but overall a decent job.
